title_guess: Phillips curve, the Friedman-Phelps long-run critique and NAIRU

elements.what: full-frame illustration of many small standing people in coloured shirts on a beige ground (about 60)
UNEMPLOYMENT in bold black on a diagonal yellow band across the crowd

segments.notes: The only full-bleed illustration in the video; a crowd stands for the unemployed.

segments.teaches: who Phillips was: in the 1950s he studied UK wage and employment data from 1861 to 1957 for his doctoral thesis

elements.what: black-and-white portrait of the economist at bottom left with his full name as a caption bar
lilac line illustration of a man working at a desk, labelled with the economist's short name
small document icon with a blue side bar before a text box
thesis note (1950s, London School of Economics) with one word highlighted yellow
UK flag above a 1861 to 1957 date range
bracket splitting into Wage and Employment, with arrows converging down onto the desk illustration

segments.notes: Real photo of a real person (BIE will not use). Data inputs drawn as two labels flowing into the researcher.

segments.teaches: his finding: a stable inverse relationship between inflation and unemployment, named the Phillips curve

elements.what: elbow arrow from the thesis note down to a second note
lilac note: evidence of a stable, inverse relation, with the two variable names coloured
small grey card titled PHILLIPS CURVE: inflation (y) vs unemployment (x), one downward-sloping convex curve
letter-spaced lilac heading at the top naming the paper's subject (unemployment vs money wage change, UK)

segments.notes: Graph first appears as a small inset card before being enlarged.

segments.teaches: reading the curve: lower unemployment comes with higher inflation; it seemed unemployment could be cut for good by accepting a little more inflation

elements.what: large inflation vs unemployment curve; a blue dot travels up the curve from low inflation/high unemployment to high inflation/low unemployment; thick coloured bars on each axis grow and shrink to show the two values; dotted drop line from the dot
white bordered box with pointer near the top of the curve: the 'permanent trade-off' idea
same portrait kept at bottom left

segments.notes: Axis bars are a neat way to show magnitudes while the point moves; reusable as a graph template.

segments.teaches: the curve became one of the most important ideas of 1960s economics

elements.what: journal-cover style picture with the year 1958, the economist's portrait and 'Phillips curve' over it
small inflation vs unemployment curve beside the cover
short caption under a black rule about its importance in the 1960s

segments.notes: Magazine-cover photo used as historical evidence.

segments.teaches: two later economists challenged the curve: the trade-off holds only in the short term

elements.what: the curve redrawn inside a pink panel with the dot near the top and axis bars
black pictograms as name puns: a man sunbathing under an umbrella (Friedman) and a diving swimmer (Phelps), names underneath
small white 'Short Term' label in the panel corner
smaller portrait kept at bottom left

segments.notes: Name-pun pictograms act as mnemonics for the two economists.

segments.teaches: why the trade-off breaks: high inflation makes workers demand higher wages, firms cannot pay everyone, firms fire workers, so unemployment returns to its natural rate in the long term

elements.what: cream box with four red statements joined by small down-arrows (inflation, wage demands, firms cannot pay, firing)
dot slides back down the curve; unemployment bar lengthens
'Short Term' struck through and 'long term' written below in a handwriting font
curved arrow from a 'Natural Rate' label up to a point on the unemployment axis

segments.notes: Strike-through of a text label (not a number) with handwritten replacement.

segments.teaches: natural rate of unemployment: the unemployment that remains when the economy uses its available resources to produce maximum output

elements.what: maroon heading at top left: natural rate of unemployment
Available Resources -> yellow ECONOMY box -> Output (GDP)
square-bullet list under the resources: technology, capital, labour
yellow outline around 'Labour'
[Max] above Output

segments.notes: Same resources -> economy -> output block reappears in E06; a reusable template.

segments.teaches: pushing unemployment below the natural rate only makes inflation keep rising; so the natural rate is also called NAIRU (non-accelerating inflation rate of unemployment)

elements.what: the heading words drift to the centre and become the graph's label
long-term pink graph restored; vertical black hatch lines added one by one in the band left of the natural rate; dot held at the natural rate
pair of black arrows pushing at the dot from both sides
NAIRU in bold maroon under a rule, with its expansion
the wage chain box kept on the right
the two name-pun pictograms kept
portrait kept

segments.notes: Restores the 141-202 composition. Hatch lines appear about once a second (accelerating inflation). Text morphs from one composition into the next.

elements.what: next-video and playlist panels
app promo: phone mock-up and app-store badges on a yellow strip
